assumptions: SPEC-070 configuration and store exist with traces.contentConsent, traces.sources and traces.retentionDays; host transcript readers and Loom and System One validators keep their current interfaces; the traces section of lightning-config.schema.json is extended (no separate consent schema); runtime stays standard-library only. Owner decisions (T001, 2026-11-13): host transcripts are an opt-in source (OD-1); emails use a per-run salted hash placeholder (OD-2); consent does not expire and status shows consentedAt (OD-3).
compatibility: Additive: default consent none keeps current behaviour; content-free telemetry unchanged; braid-lightning-config/v0.1 keys unchanged; spec069 secret patterns move to a shared module imported by the script.
domain: Braid Lightning content-bearing traces: consent, redaction, retention and purge, and adapters from rollouts, host transcripts, Loom and System One shadow episodes to triplets and messages.
execution_contract: executionAuthorization stays false; no content stored or emitted without consent redacted; redaction precedes storage; System One files are read-only and never receive adapter output; no network, subprocess or MCP tool.
hypotheses: None; engineering specification with no scientific claim.
observation_contract: Canary corpus results per pattern class and encoding; redaction counts and scan results per record; retention sweep and purge results with injected clock; byte and mtime snapshots of read-only sources before and after.

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes; no content is collected (the store gate is T003, redaction T004). Calendar validity of consentedAt (for example 2026-02-30) is checked by the validator only; the schema checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape. The per-run email salt itself is implemented with the redactor (T004).
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T002 part: traces.contentConsent accepts only none and redacted and defaults to none with a null consent record; a BL.0 profile without consentedAt and consentPreviewDigest reads as none. `lightning init --trace-consent redacted [--trace-sources ...]` previews level, consentedAt, sources (host-transcript only when listed, OD-1), retention, redaction classes (email as a per-run salted hash, OD-2), storage, residual risk and no expiry (OD-3); apply with the matching --preview-digest writes consentedAt and that digest. Unrelated changes keep the record, new sources renew it, lowering to none clears it, and `lightning status` shows level, consentedAt, sources and expires null. The schema and the validator agree on a valid and invalid corpus. Negative controls: raw, a record without consent, consent without a record, an answered record field, a stale or forged digest (nothing written), and plugin setup lab/off leave the profile byte-identical; the store still stores no content (store-consent without consent; redaction-incomplete with it, until T004).

scenarios.then: the preview shows sources, retention and effects; apply with its digest records consent; raw and stale digests are refused; schema and validator verdicts are equal
scenarios.when: consent is set to redacted through init, and the corpus is checked

requirements.text: Consent contract. traces.contentConsent accepts only none and redacted, defaults to none, and changes only through a lightning init preview applied with --apply --preview-digest (plugin setup only sets lightning off|lab); the consent fields extend the traces section of lightning-config.schema.json and that schema and the validator agree on a corpus. Consent does not expire; lightning status shows the level, consentedAt and sources.

scenarios.given: consent none and a rollout with prompt text

obtained_evidence.limits: Temporary homes; no content is read or stored. The adapter reads no source yet (T007/T008); the gate is its entry check. Content storage with consent is enabled with the redactor (T004).
obtained_evidence.outcome: passed: T003: with no profile, consent none, or an invalid profile (unparseable, redacted without its consent record, an unknown level) the store refuses a content-bearing record with store-consent and writes nothing, and the adapter gate and `lightning status` traceContent report content-consent-required; status itself refuses an invalid profile with its config-* code. An explicit content_consent none overrides a redacted profile, and an unknown explicit level is refused. With consent redacted the gate opens only for listed sources (others: source-not-consented), and the store still refuses content with redaction-incomplete because no redactor exists before T004 (C2: redact on ingest). Negative control: invalid configuration never reads as redacted. Content-free kinds are unchanged (SPEC-070 store suite).

requirements.text: Refusal without consent. With consent none or an invalid configuration, the store refuses content-bearing fields with the SPEC-070 refusal store-consent, the adapter and CLI report content-consent-required, and adapter outputs are content-free.

requirements.text: Redaction. lightning_redact replaces literal secrets, spec069 SECRET_PATTERNS, bearer and OAuth tokens, emails, home paths and API-key shapes with typed placeholders; a record whose post-scan is not clean is refused.

requirements.text: Retention and purge. A sweep deletes content records older than traces.retentionDays (default 30, max 90); the BL.0 lightning purge, extended here, deletes content for a run or all runs after a preview and leaves no content bytes.

scientific_limits: Engineering only. Catching the canary corpus does not prove every secret or personal datum is caught; pattern redaction has residual false negatives listed in the privacy review.
scope: Specification only: consent levels none and redacted recorded in lightning.json and confirmed by a lightning init preview; a redaction pipeline reusing the spec069 secret scan; retention (default 30, max 90 days) and purge; a standard-library port of TracerTraceToTriplet and TraceToMessages over rollouts, host transcripts, Loom and read-only System One episodes; an extension of the traces section of lightning-config.schema.json; privacy review.
